[notifications-service#Data]
NotificationsService: Data
It stores queued messages in the notifications Redis instance. A message stays queued until a provider accepts it or its retries run out.

[notifications-service#Overview]
NotificationsService: Overview
NotificationsService exposes the NotificationsAPI. Any service that needs to send an email, an SMS, or a push message hands it to this API instead of talking to a provider directly.

[billing-service#Integrations]
BillingService: Integrations
It depends on OrderService for line items. It calls the NotificationsAPI to send receipts once a capture succeeds.

The billing-service team also maintains the shared invoice templates.

[payments-service#Integrations]
PaymentsService: Integrations
It calls the NotificationsAPI on a declined authorization, so the customer hears about a decline even when checkout has already returned.

PaymentsService is maintained by the same team as BillingService.

[notifications-service#Operations]
NotificationsService: Operations
Provider credentials rotate monthly. During a rotation the queue keeps accepting messages and holds them until the new credentials load.

[notifications-service#Delivery and retries]
NotificationsService: Delivery and retries
Its retry semantics are three attempts with a 250ms backoff, configured by RETRY_ATTEMPTS. A message that fails all three attempts moves to the dead-letter list, and the caller is not told. Callers that need confirmation poll the message status.

[order-service#Integrations]
OrderService: Integrations
It calls the PaymentsAPI to authorize and capture. It depends on UserService to resolve the ordering customer.

[renewals-worker#Integrations]
RenewalsWorker: Integrations
It depends on BillingService and calls the PaymentsAPI directly, without going through OrderService, because a renewal has no cart.

part.text:
The affected direct callers are **BillingService** and **PaymentsService**:

| Service | Messages it sends through NotificationsAPI |
|---|---|
| **BillingService** | Receipts after a successful capture. |
| **PaymentsService** | Customer notifications after a declined authorization. |

Both call **NotificationsAPI**, exposed by **NotificationsService**, which stores queued messages in the **notifications Redis instance** until a provider accepts them or retries run out. Losing that Redis instance therefore breaks the queue-backed delivery path for both services.

Sources: `billing-service#Integrations`, `payments-service#Integrations`, `notifications-service#Overview`, and `notifications-service#Data`.
